response: Yes, the Transmissible Liability Index (TLI) assessed in late childhood has been found to predict suicidal symptoms in young adulthood. The TLI is a measure that assesses the cumulative risk of various factors, including family history, mental health, and environmental factors, that contribute to the development of psychiatric disorders. Studies have shown that a higher TLI score in late childhood is associated with an increased risk of suicidal symptoms and behaviors in young adulthood, suggesting that the TLI may be a useful tool for identifying individuals at risk and targeting early interventions to prevent suicidal behavior.
